scope: Bounded priority and theorem-delta screen of two new claims: (A) the Boolean type(rank4, weight128) exclusion and the 1-3-zero corollary; (B) the explicit 3-SAT endpoint 426679/100000. This is positioning only. No proof-correctness assertion is made, and model acceptance is not treated as review. A search miss is not novelty.
summary: A (Boolean). No inspected source excludes any quadratic residue type in the balanced nine-variable, peak<=28 setting. The candidate is therefore a not-located, conditional, partial exclusion: one of eight types. Its method family is prior art. WLW 2610.17871v1 supplies the residue and canonical-sign tools for nine variables. LXW 2610.17897v1 Props 1-3 run the same type-elimination strategy (residue quadratic Q, forced polar rank 6, forced weight 56) for hypothetical balanced eight-variable NL118 functions. LXW also derive a zero-count parity (h0 even, >=2) in that eight-variable setting, which is the nearest precedent for the corollary's parity step. The corollary (nine-variable functions with exactly 1, 2 or 3 Walsh zeros have NL<=240) was not found as a statement anywhere. Its target class is non-empty: Lou-Wang (ISIT 2024, abstract) construct a balanced nine-variable function with Walsh support F_2^9 minus {0}, and Carlet-Meaux-Broll (ePrint 2026/037, abstract) give infinite one-zero classes for n>=8. Both full texts were inaccessible, so priority stays unresolved. B (3-SAT). The endpoint 4.26679 is a same-method, same-model numerical refinement of Vorobyev's 4.268 (arXiv 2610.10599, still v1 only; repository unchanged since 2026-10-03). The difference is 0.00121, a relative improvement of 0.028%. Vorobyev's own public script already exposes the truncation cutoff and finite survey mixtures as parameters, so the refinement is routine in kind. Chatterjee et al. (v2, Section 2.6) state that a 1RSB-matching upper bound can be verified by interpolation. No earlier certified endpoint at or below 4.26679 was located; Vorobyev's 6 Oct 2026 survey lists 4.4898 as the previous best. Significance: A-main is a modest conditional partial extension, A-corollary is corollary-level with priority unresolved, and B is a modest extension.

findings.claim: A balanced nine-variable function with exactly one Walsh zero (support F_2^9 minus {0}) exists. The corollary's class is therefore non-empty, and the corollary forces NL<=240 on every such function.

findings.source: Y. Lou, Q. Wang, An Answer to an Open Problem on Balanced Boolean Functions with the Maximum Possible Walsh Supports, IEEE ISIT 2024, doi:10.1109/ISIT57864.2024.10619662
findings.access: abstract reconstructed from the OpenAlex inverted index; OpenAlex marks the work closed

findings.claim: The origin paper on Walsh supports frames the question through covering sequences and support structure. No nonlinearity-versus-zero-count statement was visible in the accessible metadata.

findings.source: Carlet and Mesnager, On the supports of the Walsh transforms of Boolean functions, ePrint 2004/256
findings.limits: The tool returned metadata only for the PDF. The body (including the n<=6 checks referenced by CMB) was not read.

findings.claim: A 2025 paper characterizes the possible Walsh-support cardinalities. Per the abstract it addresses cardinality only, not nonlinearity.

findings.source: Jauberty and Meaux, On the Cardinality of the Walsh Support of a Boolean Function, ePrint 2025/1651
findings.stance: orthogonal; suggests the corollary's 2- and 3-zero cases are non-vacuous [INFERENCE]

The candidate does the analogous type elimination for one nine-variable type.

findings.claim: Zero-count parity precedent: in the hypothetical balanced eight-variable NL118 setting, LXW prove that the number h0 of Walsh zeros is even and at least 2. The corollary needs the stronger nine-variable fact (even count, XOR zero, hence at least 4), which LXW do not state.
findings.quote: Since |supp(u)| is an integer and h₀ ≥ 1, we have h₀ ≥ 2 must be even.
findings.source: Lou-Xu-Wang, Section 3.2, after eq. (8); h_i counts Walsh coefficients of absolute value 4i
findings.stance: nearest precedent for the parity step; not the same statement

findings.claim: The known unbalanced nine-variable NL242 functions have no Walsh zeros. This is consistent with the corollary's dichotomy for peak<=28 functions: zero zeros or at least four.
findings.quote: However, there is no zero value in the Walsh spectra of these functions; hence, none of them can be linearly transformed to 9-variable balanced functions with nonlinearity 242.
findings.source: Kavut and Yucel, 9-variable Boolean Functions with Nonlinearity 242 in the Generalized Rotation Class
findings.limits: Describes the examples only; no general zero-count theorem.

findings.claim: An OpenAlex full-text search for "one Walsh zero" returns one 2026 work, by Meaux, about large Walsh co-supports and extended resilience. It is not a nonlinearity ceiling for few-zero functions.
findings.quote: These constructions yield functions with large Walsh co-supports, a necessary condition for achieving high resilience.
findings.source: P. Meaux, Extended Resilience and Walsh-Support Constructions of Boolean Functions (ORBilu green OA)
findings.limits: The ORBilu PDF fetch failed TLS certificate verification. Index coverage is not exhaustive.

The result is conditional on imported lemmas H1-H4 (canonical transform alphabet {0, ±64}; zero-moment and slack lemmas forcing an 8-point linear zero three-flat with |p| in {2,3}; Pfaffian quartic next-bit lemma).

A_main.delta: This is the first located exclusion of any residue type for balanced nine-variable peak<=28 functions: one of eight types, leaving seven. The argument components claimed as specific to this instance are the zero-three-flat geometry (1891 flats, orbit counts 1680/210/1), the 13-dimensional E-lift kernel and the fixed K-character projection energy bound (1152 > 1024 or 512). These were not located in WLW or LXW. The headline (balanced NL242) is not decided.

A_corollary.candidate: If f: F_2^9 -> F_2 has exactly 1, 2 or 3 Walsh zeros, then max|W_f| >= 32 and NL(f) <= 240. This depends on the lane's first-zero-moment lemma (zero set even with XOR zero for peak<=28 functions after a linear shift). It does not use the WLW covering-radius claim and also excludes peak 24.

Lou-Wang 2024 and Carlet-Meaux-Broll 2026 (abstracts): nine-variable one-zero functions exist; no NL statement in the abstracts.

A_corollary.delta: No located source bounds the nonlinearity of nine-variable functions by their number of Walsh zeros. Given the lemma, the corollary is a two-line consequence. Its new content is the NL<=240 ceiling for the 1-3-zero class (from the classical 244 or WLW's 242). Priority is unresolved pending the CMB and Lou-Wang full texts.

B.ours: Same model as Vorobyev: iid clauses, three distinct uniform variables, fair signs, replacement allowed. alpha = 426679/100000 at floor(alpha n) clauses. Psi_T functional with T=1024, a six-atom rational rate law, epsilon=3e-7, y=24. Two outward-rounded certifiers plus a parent-written 1536-bit checker. Written analytic bridge (model-reviewed, not formalized). McDiarmid tail.
B.antecedent: Vorobyev v1: alpha = 1067/250, T=128, law {1/20:1/4, 2/5:1/2, 17/20:1/4}, epsilon=1e-5. Lean 4 formalization per the author (release audit of 233 roots). Chebyshev O(1/n) tail.
B.numeric_delta: 4.268 - 4.26679 = 0.00121 (0.028% relative). The distance to the MMZ central value 4.26675 shrinks from 0.00125 to 0.00004 (about 97%). The lane's own floating floor for this law family is 4.2667853 at T=1024, extrapolated to about 4.266784 as T grows (lane-internal, not a source). Remaining headroom in this method is therefore about 6e-6.
B.pending: The T=128 row 213359/50000 = 4.26718 is under formal replay. If kernel-checked, it would be a formal improvement of 0.00082 on 4.268. It is not final evidence here.
B.no_earlier_endpoint_located: No exact rational or interval-certified endpoint at or below 4.26679 was found in Vorobyev's survey, arXiv listings, Chatterjee v2 or MMZ. This is a search miss.

strongest_defensible_wording.A_main: Conditional on the separately reviewed zero-set and next-residue lemmas, no balanced nine-variable Boolean function with Walsh peak at most 28 has intrinsic quadratic residue of polar rank 4 and weight 128. This excludes one of eight residue types; whether a balanced function of nonlinearity 242 exists remains open. The 2-adic residue, canonical-sign and polar-rank strategy follows Wang-Lou-Wang and Lou-Xu-Wang (arXiv, 13 Oct 2026); we did not locate this type exclusion or its zero-flat/character-projection argument in the sources checked.
strongest_defensible_wording.A_corollary: Under the same reviewed first-moment lemma, every nine-variable Boolean function with exactly one, two or three Walsh zeros has nonlinearity at most 240. Nine-variable functions with exactly one Walsh zero exist (Lou-Wang 2024; Carlet-Meaux-Broll 2026), so the statement is not vacuous. We could not read those papers in full and make no priority claim.
strongest_defensible_wording.B: In Vorobyev's model and within his energetic-interpolation framework, an explicit outward-rounded certificate (six-atom rational law, truncation T = 1024) shows that random 3-SAT is unsatisfiable with high probability at clause density 426679/100000 = 4.26679. This is 0.00121 below Vorobyev's Lean-formalized 4.268 (arXiv:2610.10599v1). The analytic bridge is written, not formalized. We located no earlier certified endpoint at or below 4.26679. This is a numerical refinement, not a new method or the threshold's location.
